title: Truck stolen by Tennessee prison escapee sat in Illinois for more than a day before it was found, police say | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

A truck that a convicted murderer stole after escaping from a Tennessee prison this week appears to have sat in southern Illinois for more than a day before police found it, authorities said, as a multistate search for him continues.

The Tennessee-registered white 2008 Ford F-350 that investigators believe Jacob Morley stole after his Sunday escape was found abandoned Tuesday in Marion, Illinois, the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation said.

The truck’s discovery is a key development in the search for 28-year-old Morley, who authorities said escaped from the Northwest Correctional Complex in the northwestern Tennessee town of Tiptonville late Sunday and stole the truck in Tennessee early Monday.

Surveillance video shows the truck appeared to have been abandoned in Marion, an Illinois city roughly a 130-mile drive north of the Tennessee prison, around 4:40 a.m. Monday, Marion police Lt. Justin Dwyer told CNN. Police found the truck around 10 a.m. Tuesday, Dwyer said.

Video evidence so far indicates Morley headed toward a highway after leaving the truck, Dwyer said.

Marion police have reviewed a handful of grainy surveillance videos that match the description of Morley but have not been able to confirm whether he is still in Marion, according to Dwyer.

“At this point we have continually searched neighborhoods, knocked on doors and followed every lead and tip that we receive. Although there is no indication he is still in Marion, we will continue to assume he is and will be on the lookout,” Dwyer said.

“All of our officers and detectives are well versed in Morley’s descriptors, photographs, etc., and will diligently canvass the area until we are confident he isn’t here or has been captured,” he said.

Morley is thesecond inmateto escape in October from the custody of the Tennessee Department of Correction, whose commissionerresignedfollowing the botched execution and hospitalization last month ofChrista Pike, who’s now back in a maximum-security prison.

Morley is now on the TBI’s “Most Wanted” list, with a combinedreward of $17,500offered by the Tennessee governor’s office, the TBI and the US Marshals Service for information leading to his arrest. His “whereabouts remain unknown, and locating him continues to be an urgent priority for law enforcement,” the TBI said Tuesday.

“Our law enforcement partners in surrounding states have been notified to be on the lookout,” the TBI said in a release Wednesday, adding its agents “continue to assist our local, state, and federal partners in locating Jacob Morley.”

Illinois State Police has offered its assistance to the TBI and the Marion Police Department but is not leading the investigation, Sgt. Melissa Albert-Lopez, a spokesperson for the agency, told CNN.

Morley escaped through a fence at the prison in Tiptonville, a Tennessee town near the state lines with Missouri and Kentucky, late Sunday, with staff realizing he was missing around 11:30 p.m., according to the Tennessee Department of Correction.

Security camera footage later revealed Morley “breached the perimeter fence” and left the facility wearing his prison uniform, the department said. He then stole the truck early Monday in Lake County, where Tiptonville is situated, the TBI said.

He had been sentenced to life in prison after being convicted of first-degree murder, aggravated burglary, tampering with evidence, evading arrest and vandalism.

In Marion, Illinois, a small city of about17,600 people, one resident told CNN, “It’s a scary time.”

“Everybody is locking their car doors now,” Bridget Lawler, a local attorney, said Wednesday morning. “I know my husband checked all of our doors before he went to bed.”

Another resident said she did not receive an alert from local authorities. “No one that I have talked to has mentioned seeing it either. We only got information through Facebook,” Lachelle Hartline told CNN.

Marion police said they notified the public through local media outlets.

Morley was convicted in the killing of Cody Birchfield, who was initially reported missing in February 2022, according to theCarter CountySheriff’s Office.

Birchfield’s body was found weeks after he went missing, in a box under Morley’s house,The Associated Pressreported.

Birchfield’s older sister said her brother was always there for his family. “It didn’t matter when, where, or what you needed,” Carrie Norman told CNN affiliate WCYB.

Finding out her brother’s killer had escaped was jarring, she added.

“You feel sick to your stomach … it’s all those feelings come rushing back,” she said.

A cousin of Birchfield’s, who asked not to be named for safety reasons, told CNN that Morley’s life sentence gave the family “a small sense of closure and the reassurance that justice had been served.” But learning of his escape has reopened their “deepest wounds.”

The cousin said the family’s primary concerns are public safety and keeping attention on Morley’s escape, urging anyone with information that could help authorities to come forward.

But the family also wants the focus to remain on Birchfield.

“Above all, we want Cody to be remembered not for the tragedy of his death, but for the warmth, kindness, and decency of his life,” the cousin said.

Another cousin of Birchfield’s, who also asked to speak anonymously for safety reasons, told CNN they’re worried about the safety of his father and sister, who still live in the same area.

“If that man can do that to my cousin, what’s he going to do to the next individual?” the cousin said.

“Morley could be anywhere,” TBI said in a release Thursday afternoon. “We are asking Tennesseans, as well as community members in surrounding states, to remain vigilant.”
